title: Search Autocomplete Suggestions
statement:
Return up to three lexicographically smallest product names matching each typed prefix of a search query.

Contract
- `products` is a non-null array of distinct, non-empty lowercase ASCII product names. Do not mutate the input array.
- `query` is a non-null, non-empty lowercase ASCII string.
- Return a `List<List<String>>` of size `query.length()`. Entry `i` (`0 <= i < query.length()`) contains at most `3` names from `products` that start with `query.substring(0, i + 1)`, ordered lexicographically.
- If fewer than three products match a prefix, include all matching products; if none match, include an empty list.

Examples
- `suggest(["mobile", "mouse", "moneypot", "monitor", "mousepad"], "mouse")` returns:
  - `"m"` -> `["mobile", "moneypot", "monitor"]`
  - `"mo"` -> `["mobile", "moneypot", "monitor"]`
  - `"mou"` -> `["mouse", "mousepad"]`
  - `"mous"` -> `["mouse", "mousepad"]`
  - `"mouse"` -> `["mouse", "mousepad"]`
- `suggest(["haven"], "haven")` returns `["haven"]` for each of the 5 prefixes.
- `suggest(["bag", "ball"], "cat")` returns three empty lists.
hints: Copy and sort the product names lexicographically first; all names sharing any prefix then occupy a single contiguous range.
As each character of query is typed, the matching range [left, right] only narrows—advance left while sorted[left] does not match query[i], and pull right inward while sorted[right] does not match.
At each step, take at most three items starting at left (up to right). Intended complexity: O(n log n) time to sort and narrow the window, and O(n) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: product1, product2 | query, for example: mobile, mouse, moneypot, monitor, mousepad | mouse
sampleInput: mobile, mouse, moneypot, monitor, mousepad | mouse
